crossing supervisor Listen Share on Facebook Share on Twitter Print Content components School crossing supervisors have a much-valued role in Boroondara. On an average school day in Boroondara, they help 9,266 pedestrians to cross the street while 74,426 motor vehicles use our roads during school crossing times. We are always looking for school crossing supervisors. If you are friendly, reliable and flexible, this role is for you. What does a school crossing supervisor do? This paid position gives you the opportunity to get involved in your community and improve road safety for children, people with a disability and the general public who use our 114 school crossings. School crossing supervisors: • work part-time Monday to Friday, from 8 am to 9 am and from 3 pm to 4 pm, during the school term • play an important role in educating children with ‘Stop, Look and Listen’ instructions • are responsible for reporting any road hazards or potential risks • help to encourage active and independent travel. About you We are looking for people aged 18 and older who: • can attend shifts at short notice • have their own reliable transport • are able to work across several locations • can complete the pre-employment medical and police checks. You will have access to a full training program before starting your role. Submit an online application through our Careers website . Attend an interview – meet with one of our Council Officers at Council, located at 8 Inglesby Road in Camberwell. Provide us with relevant employment documents – including your Working With Children Check, Police Check and evidence of your COVID-19 vaccination status. Complete a medical assessment. Apply to become a School Crossings Supervisor We are always recruiting new school crossing supervisors to help people to cross our roads safely at peak school times. A little bit about the role The Knowledge Specialist will have a key role in supporting our Customer Connect team by ensuring frontline staff have access to clear, accurate and practical operational guidance so every customer has a helpful, responsive and seamless experience. In this role, you will review existing documentation, training materials and processes, and transform this into simple, engaging and user-friendly content. You will also lead the development of structured training materials that our operational trainers can deliver confidently and effectively. Through analysis of operational data, quality outcomes, and frontline feedback, the Knowledge Specialist will identify trends and improvement opportunities to enhance both customer experience and operational efficiency, and contribute to a strong culture of continuous improvement. Key deliverables and responsibilities include: The identification of current knowledge sources to consolidate into a single source of truth, removing duplication and making knowledge accessible and easy to find Review and update SharePoint knowledge articles using a consistent format Translation of complex policies and processes into clear, concise and engaging guidance Work closely with frontline teams, team leaders, trainers and other stakeholders to capture operational knowledge and inform improvements Create content that helps teams navigate systems, provide accurate information and follow up with customers effectively Maintaining strong governance, version control and documentation standards A little bit about you You will be naturally curious, customer focused and love making complex information simple with high attention to detail and a commitment to accuracy and governance. To be successful in this role you will have: Experience in process improvement, knowledge management, training development or operational support within a customer service or contact centre environment Strong process mapping and documentation skills, with the ability to develop and continuously improve knowledge base content and standard operating procedures Business acumen and data analysis capability to identify trends and improvement opportunities Experience supporting change management and driving improvement initiatives High level stakeholder engagement and communication skills, using plain language Proven experience developing clear, engaging documentation and training materials suitable for delivery by non-specialist trainers High attention to detail and a commitment to accuracy and governance The ability to identify and apply practical AI-enabled tools to improve knowledge access and enhance frontline capability Want to know more You can connect further and gain a better insight into this opportunity by reviewing the Position Description Employment requirements Applicants must have the right to work in Australia Preferred applicants will be required to undergo a National Police Record Check How to apply If you are passionate about customer experience, continuous improvement and building the capability of others looking to make a meaningful contribution, we would love to hear from you. Skip to Main Content Career Opportunities: Library Officer (Customer Support) (15325) Requisition ID 15325 - Posted - Job Function (1) - Tenure Status (1) - Employment Status (1)  Job Description Print Preview Apply Save Job Email Job to Friend Return to List Library Officer (Customer Support) Part-time permanent position (14hrs per week over Monday, Tuesday & Thursday ) Fantastic opportunity to join our dynamic Library Services team! $78,621 - $84,734 Band 4 (pro rata to be applied) plus Superannuation This position is primarily based at the Greythorn Library Lounge but is expected to work across all library location as needed If you enjoy working with people, thrive in a busy customer service environment and have outstanding interpersonal skills,, this may be the perfect opportunity for you. Join our dynamic library service and play a key role in creating positive experiences for our community. Please note that all positions require regular evening and weekend work. A little bit about the role The Library Officer (Customer Support) plays an important role in delivering outstanding customer experiences across our library service. Working collaboratively with the Customer Support team and broader library staff, this position supports the day-to-day delivery of library services by assisting customers with enquiries, managing circulation and membership transactions, and promoting library collections, programs and events. Through friendly, responsive and professional service, the Library Officer helps create a welcoming and engaging environment for all library users. What will you bring to the role? We are seeking a motivated and customer-focused individual to join our team and help deliver exceptional library experiences for the Boroondara community. You will be passionate about providing outstanding customer service, enjoy working with a diverse range of people, and thrive in a collaborative environment. To be successful in this role you will have: Well-developed interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to engage effectively with people from diverse backgrounds. Experience in a frontline customer service role; experience in a public library environment will be highly regarded. Strong problem-solving skills, with the ability to adapt, learn and respond to changing situations. Effective time management and organisational skills, with the ability to prioritise work and respond to customer demand. A positive, proactive approach and a commitment to delivering high-quality customer experiences. The successful applicant will also have: A relevant post-secondary qualification Confidence using a variety of digital devices and consumer technologies. Strong computer skills, including experience with Microsoft Office applications and online systems. The ability to lift, push or carry library resources around library facilities (subject to appropriate Occupational Health and Safety regulations), and A current driver's license (advantageous). Employment Requirements Applicants must have the right to work in Australia. Preferred applicants will be required to undergo a National Police Record Check and hold a valid Working with Children Clearance. Subject to a satisfactory medical check How to Apply Please submit your application online via the ‘ Apply’ button by 04 December 2026 . All applications must be made via the online portal; no applications direct to the hiring manager will be considered. No calls or applications from agencies please. We encourage you to submit your application early, if there is sufficient response, the advertisement period may close earlier than 04 December 2026 For any further information please refer to the position description , or contact Gitte Mortensen during business hours on 9278 4339 for a confidential discussion. If you want to know more about the benefits of working for the City of Boroondara, please visit our Careers Website. As part of our Technology Platforms team, you'll play a key role in ensuring our business applications effectively support Council services, business processes and strategic priorities. We are seeking a collaborative and customer-focused Functional Analyst to provide functional support, business analysis expertise and stakeholder engagement across a diverse range of enterprise applications. About the role Reporting to the Lead Analyst, you will act as the vital link between business users, service owners, vendors and technical teams. You'll develop a strong understanding of Council's business applications and processes, helping to resolve issues, support enhancements, gather requirements and improve system outcomes across the organisation. Key responsibilities include: Providing day-to-day functional support and troubleshooting for business applications. Gathering, analysing and documenting business and functional requirements. Conducting process mapping, impact assessments and gap analysis activities. Supporting system changes, testing and implementation activities. Developing and maintaining user guides, process documentation and other functional artefacts. Building strong relationships with stakeholders across Council and external vendors. Providing trusted advice on application functionality, enhancements and business process improvements. Contributing to system roadmaps, upgrades and continuous improvement initiatives. About you We're looking for someone who combines strong analytical thinking with excellent stakeholder engagement skills. You will bring: Experience in a Functional Analyst, Business Analyst, Application Support or similar role. Strong understanding of how business processes are enabled by technology. Experience troubleshooting application issues and coordinating resolutions. Proven capability in requirements gathering, documentation and business analysis. Experience with process mapping, testing and supporting system change. Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to work effectively with both technical and non-technical stakeholders. A strong customer focus and commitment to continuous improvement. The ability to quickly learn new systems and business processes. Desirable experience includes: Microsoft SharePoint, Power Apps and Power Automate. ERP and/or CRM platforms. Local government or public sector environments. Enterprise systems commonly used within local government. Why join us? At City of Boroondara, you'll be part of an organisation driven by innovation, integrity, collaboration and customer focus. Skip to Main Content Career Opportunities: Local Laws Officer (15320) Requisition ID 15320 - Posted - Job Function (1) - Tenure Status (1) - Employment Status (1)  Job Description Print Preview Apply Save Job Email Job to Friend Return to List 2 x full-time opportunities available (1 x ongoing and 1 x 12 months fixed term) $93,845 -101,184 per annum (plus super) Tool of trade vehicle provided (non-hybrid position) Join us in building a professional investigations team and help deliver a responsive, community-focused Local Laws service. In this role, you will contribute to a safe, liveable and well-maintained municipality while providing high-quality regulatory service to residents and stakeholders. About the role At City of Boroondara, our Local Laws directly contributes to our purpose of protecting the health, safety, amenity and assets of the municipality. Based within the large and busy department of Civic Services, the team works as part of five field-based teams and many others within the Urban Living Directorate. You will respond to reported breaches of the Amenity Local Law and the Environment Protection Act, using education, investigation and enforcement to achieve compliance. The role involves managing a varied caseload, gathering evidence, preparing clear records and working within established procedures to resolve matters fairly and effectively. The position includes investigating issues such as illegally dumped rubbish under the EPA, unsightly properties, overhanging vegetation, illegally advertising and the occupation of Council land, while providing courteous and timely service to community members. From time to time, you will also support the Animal Management team with park patrols, asset protection team with related after-hours complaints and work with external stakeholders including Victoria Police, the Magistrates’ Court and Council prosecutors. Hours are allocated over a 16-week roster (42-hours per week) and rotating weekend work is required every 4 weeks with penalty rates that convert into an annualised salary. A fully maintained vehicle is provided as a ‘tool of trade’ to perform necessary duties and commute to and from work. This is a non-hybrid role as our ‘office’ is in the community, every day and our success comes from working together with other officers, as a team! About you We are looking for someone who brings sound judgement, a strong customer focus and a collaborative approach. You will be supported to build your knowledge and succeed in the role. You will have experience delivering customer service in a complex regulatory environment or another fast-paced setting, with the ability to communicate clearly, build rapport and respond professionally in a range of situations under pressure. Experience in areas such as retail, hospitality, community services or other enforcement role can provide a strong foundation for success in this role. You will be able to investigate issues methodically, collect information accurately and prepare clear notes and reports. Knowledge of compliance, local laws or related legislation will be well regarded, as will the ability to interpret policy and apply it in practical situations. If you are still developing in these areas, a willingness to learn will be equally valued. Success in this role also requires respectful negotiation skills, sound problem-solving and judgement skills, de-escalating interpersonal situations with members of the community, and the capacity to work across the community each day, including walking for extended periods and assisting with animal handling when required. A qualification in enforcement, local laws, justice or a related field is desirable, but not essential. Want to know more? View the Position description What sets us apart? An investment in your ongoing professional and personal development You will be part of a team that makes a real difference. Working at Boroondara means contributing to creating positive change in the world. Join us in a role where your work matters, and you contribute to meaningful outcomes. A supportive and friendly workplace culture that values diversity, collaboration and continuous improvement. We offer many staff benefits such as flexible working arrangements, study support, wellbeing programs, gym and pool memberships Employment requirements Applicants must have the right to work in Australia. Preferred applicants will be required to undergo a National Police Record Check. How to Apply Follow these steps, carefully: Please submit your application online via the ‘ Apply ’ button by 11.59pm , Sunday 29 November 2026. Ensure you address your cover letter to Harry Mellos and answer the following questions: What about the Local Laws Officer role motivates you? Why is this the next logical step in your career? We are seeking skilled and experienced professional care workers who love supporting people to live independently in the community. We currently provide services in Mount Alexander Shire and Central Goldfields Shire. This is your opportunity to bring your passion and skills to be part of a professional and dedicated team providing high quality in-home support to frail older people and people with disabilities in our community. The role provides tailored services to help clients live healthy, independent and active lives through assistance with daily tasks and activities. Direct Care Worker Traineeship Opportunities: If you don’t already have a certificate III in Individual Support, you can also apply here for a Trainee Direct Care Worker position, to earn and learn on the job. Minimum Qualifications and Experience You must have, or be willing to obtain: Current Police Check Current Working with Children Check Triple vaccinated for COVID (2 doses plus a booster). Current Drivers license and roadworthy, registered and comprehensively insured vehicle for work travel Applicants must be able to work weekends. First Aid and CPR certificate will be gained though training and applied to the role as required If you have any queries or would like to discuss the role, the key contacts are: Sarah Newstead In Home Support Coordinator – East (03) 5471 1845 Talia Jenkin In Home Support Coordinator – West (03) 5471 1728 To apply for a Direct Care Worker or Direct Care Worker Trainee position, please provide a cover letter (no more than 2 pages) outlining why you are interested and the best candidate for this role, and your current resume. Additional information Mount Alexander Shire Council is committed to providing a safe, inclusive, and respectful workplace. We are an equal opportunity employer and are committed to child safety with zero tolerance for child abuse. We value a diverse workforce and encourage applicants from all cultures, sexual orientations, gender identities and backgrounds. Applicants can expect that the recruitment process will include interviewing, reference checks and criminal history checks. Some positions will also be required to provide a Working with Children Check, and medical assessments including drug and alcohol testing may be undertaken. For more information on the recruitment process, please download the Candidate information document from our website.
